prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: hospital automated medication dispensing/returns: order intake, pharmacy prep/verification, cold chain, tube transport, ward cabinets, returns, dose exceptions. Aliases: Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Elements: Gateway (validates orders; rejects incomplete/inconsistent updates, retains reason; Order Reconciliation Snapshot; status; routes to review). Robot (prepares authorized orders; Priority Refill Tote Tag; presents package to Station; on exception stops pick, holds package, preserves scanned product/quantity data). Station (compares order vs scanned product/strength/quantity, blocks on mismatch; Batch Release Note; records exception category/evidence/disposition/reviewer on Dose Exception Review Slip). Cooler (temperature records; reports excursions/connectivity loss; displays to staff; affected stock unavailable pending assessment). East/West Tube Dispatch Consoles (route availability; monitor capsules; Tube Route Exception Ticket). Pneumatic Tube Network (compliant loads only; segment unavailable until tested). North/South Ward Cabinet Controllers (record arrival time/cabinet; states Ready for Dispense, Out of Service; North confirms ward via tote tag, blocks held transactions until disposition; South reports failed lock/unrecognized access). Return Kiosk (guides bin checks; Return Bin Audit Label, used by Technician). Actors: Clinical Pharmacist (Dose Exception Review Slip; assesses dose/route/timing/patient concerns; approves correction or rejects). Pharmacy Technician (prep; ID checks; Cold Chain Handoff Card; gathers evidence, no clinical decisions). Medication Safety Officer (Diversion Review Packet). Registered Nurse (verifies ward load, cold handling, return eligibility; keeps held transaction locked, confirms not administered; escalates urgent concerns to Pharmacist; never bypasses hold/substitutes). Charge Nurse (Cabinet Downtime Notice; assigns unresolved discrepancies/exceptions to named role across handover). Hospital Courier (Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record; collects only closed, ready-recorded bins). Biomedical Engineer, IT Operations Specialist. Requirements: discrepancies block prep; release linked to order ID, package ID, time, credentials; canceled/duplicate/superseded held; capsule IDs reconciled before admission; route/packaging problems hold load; staff keep custody if transfer unavailable; ward receipt checks

New part:
S140: The Medication Safety Officer reviews suspected diversion, repeated high-risk exceptions, and events with potential for patient harm.
S141: IT Operations Specialist receives the Diversion Review Packet and checks access, transaction, and device logs without changing the clinical disposition.
S142: The Biomedical Engineer evaluates a suspected mechanical or sensor fault and advises whether the affected equipment can safely return to service.
S143: The IT Operations Specialist investigates software or connectivity faults and records the technical findings for the responsible operational team.
S144: A serious or time-critical exception is escalated immediately by the observing staff member rather than held for routine review.
S145: If the clinical review remains inconclusive, the transaction stays on hold and the Clinical Pharmacist seeks a higher-level clinical decision.
S146: The final disposition records who reviewed the exception, what evidence supported the decision, and whether the medication was released, corrected, or withheld.
S147: Morrowglass validates each medication order for patient, product, dose, route, and timing fields before making it available for downstream processing.
S148: Copperfield confirms that the reconciliation queue has no unresolved discrepancy before authorizing routine cabinet replenishment.
S149: Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot uses the Order Reconciliation Snapshot to compare requested quantities with completed dispense events and current cabinet balances.
S150: Reconciliation compares the active order record with dispensing and cabinet records using a stable order identifier.
S151: The comparison preserves the order context needed to distinguish a new request from a correction or a repeat submission.
S152: Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot retains the patient, medication, dose, route, and timing details associated with each order while preparing a dispense transaction.
S153: It also checks whether the order is active and whether its authorization remains valid at the time of processing.
S154: A cancelled order is excluded from routine preparation even when a matching dispense request remains in a local queue.
S155: A corrected order is treated as a new authoritative version, and superseded values are not carried forward.
S156: Duplicate submissions are flagged for review rather than converted into additional cabinet quantity.
S157: Partial dispensing is reconciled against the quantity already recorded so that remaining quantity is calculated conservatively.
S158: Time stamps and transaction identifiers are retained to support comparison across records that arrive at different times.
S159: When the records disagree on patient, medication, or quantity, the affected transaction remains on hold until the discrepancy is resolved.
S160: The reconciliation outcome records the matched values, unresolved differences, and disposition for subsequent audit.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
